samples.summary: The renamed `__oauthState` → `opts.state` forwarding in GitHubStrategy.authenticate has no test at all
samples.evidence: The diff renames the request-attached state key from `__cliStateToken` to `__oauthState` in `github.strategy.ts:61-67`, and this is now the single hinge of the whole CSRF design (both CLI and browser states reach GitHub only through it). `github.strategy.spec.ts` (read in full, 119 lines) tests only endpoint resolution — it never constructs a request or asserts `super.authenticate` received `state`. Grep for `__oauthState` across packages/backend/src returns only the guard, the guard spec (which asserts the guard *sets* it) and the strategy itself; no test asserts the strategy *reads* that key. If the two sides ever spelled the key differently, every login would reach GitHub stateless and the new callback guard would reject every callback, with a fully green backend suite.

samples.summary: The confirmation page's preservation of `nonce` and `port` into the Continue href is untested
samples.evidence: `renderConfirmPage` re-encodes `mode`, `port`, `nonce` and `confirm` into the Continue link (cli-login-confirm.middleware.ts:100-103); that link is the only way the CLI's per-attempt nonce survives the new confirmation hop to the guard. In `cli-login-confirm.middleware.spec.ts` the page-rendering test (line 43-56) passes NO nonce and asserts only `Continue` and `confirm=<secret>`; the test that does supply a nonce (line 58) takes the already-confirmed branch and never inspects any HTML. So `if (nonce) params.set('nonce', nonce)` and the port round-trip are unasserted: drop the nonce from the href and the CLI login silently breaks (loopback refuses with 'no `state`') while every test stays green.

samples.summary: AuthModule's new middleware wiring (`configure`) is not covered by any test
samples.evidence: `AuthModule.configure` applies `CliLoginConfirmMiddleware` to `GET auth/github`. The middleware spec instantiates the class directly (`new CliLoginConfirmMiddleware()`), so it proves nothing about registration; grep for `CliLoginConfirmMiddleware` finds it only in auth.module.ts and its own spec, and grep for `auth/github` under packages/backend/test finds only a callback URL constant in integration-helpers. No Nest testing-module or e2e test asserts the gate actually runs on that route, so unwiring it (or mis-specifying the path/method) breaks the confirmation gate with a green suite.

samples.summary: Web-flow failure tests never assert the single-use state cookie is cleared on mismatch
samples.evidence: auth.controller.ts:142-145 clears `wafflebase_oauth_state` before comparing, so the cookie is spent even on a failed match. Only the success test asserts `res.clearCookie` was called; the two rejection tests ('rejects a state that does not match the cookie', 'rejects a state presented without the cookie') assert only `res.cookie` was not called. Moving the clear below the throw (leaving a replayable cookie) would not fail any test.

samples.summary: The `parseOutputFormat`-before-request ordering is asserted only for files/tabs/api-keys/status; docs, notes, slides and sheets-import got the same change with no test
samples.evidence: The diff adds pre-request `parseOutputFormat` calls to api-keys, cells, ctx, docs, files, notes, schema, sheets-import, slides, status and tabs, but grep for INVALID_FORMAT/parseOutputFormat in packages/cli/test matches only status.test.ts, tabs.test.ts, files-format.test.ts, api-keys.test.ts and output.test.ts. The mutating commands `docs rename/delete`, `notes rename/delete`, `slides rename/delete` and `sheets import` — the ones where a late throw would discard a completed write, which is the stated reason for the change — have no ordering test.

samples.summary: No unit test exercises `formatCsv(..., { neutralizeFormulas: false })`
samples.evidence: Every `formatCsv` call in packages/cli/test/output.test.ts passes `{ neutralizeFormulas: true }`; the raw branch is covered only indirectly by test/sheets-export.test.ts via `--raw`. Adequate but the option's false path has no direct unit assertion (e.g. that quoting still applies without neutralizing).

finding.summary: The renamed `__oauthState` → `opts.state` forwarding in GitHubStrategy.authenticate has no test at all
finding.evidence: The diff renames the request-attached state key from `__cliStateToken` to `__oauthState` in `github.strategy.ts:61-67`, and this is now the single hinge of the whole CSRF design (both CLI and browser states reach GitHub only through it). `github.strategy.spec.ts` (read in full, 119 lines) tests only endpoint resolution — it never constructs a request or asserts `super.authenticate` received `state`. Grep for `__oauthState` across packages/backend/src returns only the guard, the guard spec (which asserts the guard *sets* it) and the strategy itself; no test asserts the strategy *reads* that key. If the two sides ever spelled the key differently, every login would reach GitHub stateless and the new callback guard would reject every callback, with a fully green backend suite.

verdict.reason: No test anywhere in the repository exercises GitHubStrategy.authenticate's forwarding of req.__oauthState into the passport options. github.strategy.spec.ts (119 lines) covers only enterprise endpoint resolution — it never builds a request nor spies on super.authenticate. github-auth.guard.spec.ts asserts only that the guard *writes* req.__oauthState, and it explicitly mocks the passport prototype canActivate (line 48) so the strategy never executes. A repo-wide grep (excluding node_modules) for `super.authenticate|.authenticate(` yields only github.strategy.ts:67 and a doc comment; no backend e2e spec hits GET /auth/github (the only `github` matches under packages/backend/test are env fixtures in helpers). The CLI-side `state` assertions in packages/cli/test are about the loopback callback, and auth.controller.spec.ts covers the callback-side validation, not the outbound hand-off. Because the reader uses an inline cast `(req as { __oauthState?: string })` while the guard writes to an untyped `req`, a key-spelling divergence would not be caught by the type checker either — the behavior is untested end-to-end and a regression would leave the suite green.

finding.summary: The confirmation page's preservation of `nonce` and `port` into the Continue href is untested
finding.evidence: `renderConfirmPage` re-encodes `mode`, `port`, `nonce` and `confirm` into the Continue link (cli-login-confirm.middleware.ts:100-103); that link is the only way the CLI's per-attempt nonce survives the new confirmation hop to the guard. In `cli-login-confirm.middleware.spec.ts` the page-rendering test (line 43-56) passes NO nonce and asserts only `Continue` and `confirm=<secret>`; the test that does supply a nonce (line 58) takes the already-confirmed branch and never inspects any HTML. So `if (nonce) params.set('nonce', nonce)` and the port round-trip are unasserted: drop the nonce from the href and the CLI login silently breaks (loopback refuses with 'no `state`') while every test stays green.

verdict.reason: Verified independently. renderConfirmPage (cli-login-confirm.middleware.ts:95-103) encodes mode/port/nonce/confirm into the Continue href, and that href is the only carrier of the CLI nonce across the new confirmation hop. The sole test that inspects the rendered HTML (cli-login-confirm.middleware.spec.ts:43-56) supplies no nonce and asserts only that the HTML contains 'Continue' and `confirm=<secret>`; neither the nonce nor the port round-trip is asserted. The only nonce-bearing test (spec:58-72) takes the already-confirmed branch, so res.send is never invoked and no HTML is examined; the other two rendering tests (spec:74-83, 85-94) assert only next/__cliConfirmed/res.send. Searching wider found no counterexample: renderConfirmPage is imported by no test (repo-wide grep, only its own definition and call site at line 85); github-auth.guard.spec.ts only sets/checks __cliConfirmed (lines 55, 96); auth.controller.spec.ts:215-241 covers the downstream nonce->state echo but constructs state directly via cliAuthStore.createState, bypassing the page; packages/backend/test/*.e2e-spec.ts never hits /auth/github (only a callback URL constant in helpers/integration-helpers.ts:94); packages/cli/test contains no confirm-page handling; no snapshot files exist in packages/backend. Removing `if (nonce) params.set('nonce', nonce)` leaves the whole suite green while breaking CLI login, so this is a real behavior of the new hop with no meaningful coverage — major under the missing-tests branch of the test-adequacy rubric.
